title: General Uniform Fiber Transfer: uniformOn Preserved for All Events
description: Answers OQ-01-OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-02: Generalizes uniformOn_fiber_transfer from one specific ballot event to ALL events simultaneously. Proves: if f : α → β is surjective from A onto T (finite sets) with uniform fiber sizes k, then for ANY P ⊆ T, uniformOn A (f⁻¹'P) = uniformOn T P. 8 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext:
The classical ballot problem (Bertrand 1887, Désiré André 1887) asks for the probability that candidate A stays strictly ahead of B throughout the counting of a ballot. The modern treatment via Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn` reformulates this combinatorially: ballot sequences form a finite set with a uniform measure, and the ballot theorem follows from a fiber-transfer argument showing that the projection onto final tallies preserves conditional probabilities.

The OQ chain ballot-problem-oq-01 through oq-01-oq-02-oq-01 progressively abstracted this argument: OQ-01 proved the classical result, OQ-01-OQ-02 proved the multi-candidate generalization, and OQ-01-OQ-02-OQ-01 extracted the key mechanism as `uniformOn_fiber_transfer` — showing that the ballot projection preserves uniformOn for one specific event. This final OQ-01-OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-02 asks the natural mathematical question: is the fiber-transfer result for one event actually a *universal* property?

The answer YES places the ballot probability argument in the general theory of probability-preserving maps. In measure theory, a measure-preserving map between probability spaces satisfies $\mu(f^{-1}(E)) = \nu(E)$ for ALL measurable events E — not just some special one. The equal-fiber surjection condition is precisely the discrete-finite analog: $|A \cap f^{-1}(\{t\})| = k$ for all $t \in T$ is the condition that makes $f$ an isomorphism of discrete probability spaces (under `uniformOn`). The passage from singleton events to all events is enabled by Finset sum additivity: $|A \cap f^{-1}(P)| = \sum_{t \in P} |A \cap f^{-1}(\{t\})| = k|P|$, and dividing by $|A| = k|T|$ cancels the fiber-size factor $k$. This theorem is the discrete-finite-set instance of the general pushforward measure identity $f_* \mu = \nu$.
overview.problemStatement: Can the uniformOn_fiber_transfer pattern be generalized: if a surjective map between finite probability spaces has uniform fibers, does it preserve all event probabilities (not just uniformOn)?
overview.text: YES — uniform fiber surjections preserve uniformOn for ALL events. For any finite sets A, T, any surjection f : A → T with uniform fiber size k, and any event P ⊆ T: uniformOn A (f⁻¹'P) = uniformOn T P.
overview.proofStrategy: Fiber decomposition gives A = ⋃_{t∈T} (A ∩ f⁻¹'{t}) (using surjectivity) and A ∩ f⁻¹'P = ⋃_{t∈P} (A ∩ f⁻¹'{t}). Uniform counting (ncard_biUnion_eq_of_uniform) gives ncard(A) = k·ncard(T) and ncard(A ∩ f⁻¹'P) = k·ncard(P). The factor k cancels in the ENNReal ratio.
keyInsights: The fiber decomposition argument works for ANY P ⊆ T, not just the specific ballot event — the key is that uniform fiber sizes allow the cancellation of k in numerator and denominator
SurjOn is needed to prove ncard(A) = k·ncard(T): without surjectivity, there could be 'missing' fibers
The abstract version uses ncard_biUnion_eq_of_uniform from BallotFiberTransfer, making the proof modular
Complement and union corollaries follow immediately from the main theorem — no additional work needed
The proof works for ANY α, β types with Finite hypotheses — it is fully type-parametric

The cancellation of k is the conceptual heart: ncard(A∩f⁻¹'P)/ncard(A) = k·|P|/k·|T| = |P|/|T|. This telescoping makes the equal-fiber condition precisely the right hypothesis — not stronger, not weaker.

This is the discrete analog of a measure-preserving map: uniform-fiber surjections are probability-algebra homomorphisms that preserve all event probabilities, just as measure-preserving maps between probability spaces preserve all measure values.

sections.title: Module Introduction: Open Question and Proof Strategy
sections.summary: Module docstring poses OQ-01-OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-02 (generalize uniformOn_fiber_transfer to ALL events) and answers YES. Describes the four-step proof strategy: S-decomposition via surjectivity, P-fiber decomposition, uniform counting via ncard_biUnion_eq_of_uniform, ENNReal ratio cancellation. Contrasts with OQ-01: that proved one event for one function; this proves ALL events for ANY function with uniform fibers.
sections.mathContext: The key abstraction step: generalize from a specific ballot event $P_0$ to $\forall P \subseteq T: \text{uniformOn}(S)(f^{-1}(P)) = \text{uniformOn}(T)(P)$. The proof works because $k$ cancels: $\frac{k|P|}{k|T|} = \frac{|P|}{|T|}$.

sections.title: Fiber Geometry Lemmas
sections.summary: preimage_inter_eq_iUnion: A ∩ f⁻¹'P decomposes as ⋃ t∈P, A ∩ f⁻¹'{t}. surjOn_fiber_decomp: A decomposes as ⋃ t∈T, A ∩ f⁻¹'{t} when f is surjective. singleton_fiber_disjoint: distinct singletons give disjoint fibers.
sections.mathContext: $A \cap f^{-1}(P) = \bigcup_{t \in P} (A \cap f^{-1}(\{t\}))$ — the preimage of P decomposes into fibers over singletons, which are pairwise disjoint.

sections.title: Uniform Fiber Counting
sections.summary: uniform_fiber_count: (A ∩ f⁻¹'P).ncard = k * P.ncard when fibers have uniform size k over T. Uses ncard_biUnion_eq_of_uniform from the parent.
sections.mathContext: $|A \cap f^{-1}(P)| = k \cdot |P|$ when $|A \cap f^{-1}(\{t\})| = k$ for all $t \in T$ and $P \subseteq T$.

sections.title: Main Theorem: General Uniform Fiber Transfer
sections.summary: uniformOn_fiber_transfer_all: MAIN — for any surjection with uniform fibers, uniformOn A (f⁻¹'P) = uniformOn T P for ALL P ⊆ T. Proof: fiber counting gives ncard(A) = k·ncard(T) and ncard(A∩f⁻¹'P) = k·ncard(P), factor k cancels via ENNReal.div_eq_div_iff.
sections.mathContext: For surjective $f : A \to T$ with $|A \cap f^{-1}(\{t\})| = k$ for all $t \in T$: $\text{uniformOn}(A)(f^{-1}(P)) = \frac{|A \cap f^{-1}(P)|}{|A|} = \frac{k|P|}{k|T|} = \frac{|P|}{|T|} = \text{uniformOn}(T)(P)$.

sections.title: Corollaries: All-Events, Complement, Union
sections.summary: uniformOn_preserves_all_events: universal quantification over all P. uniformOn_complement_transfer: the complement T\P is also transferred. uniformOn_union_transfer: finite unions P∪Q are transferred.
sections.mathContext: The main theorem immediately gives: complements, unions, and all Boolean combinations of events are preserved. This confirms that the map f is probability-preserving in the fullest sense for the discrete uniform distribution.

conclusion.summary: Proves the general uniform fiber transfer theorem: any surjection with equal fiber sizes preserves uniformOn for all events simultaneously. This answers OQ-01-OQ-02-OQ-01-OQ-02 with YES. Machine-verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: This result establishes that equal-fiber surjections are the discrete-finite-set analogue of measure-preserving maps: they are isomorphisms of discrete probability spaces. Combined with the ballot OQ-01 result, the full OQ chain gives a complete modular picture — the ballot theorem is an instance of a universal structural property rather than a combinatorial coincidence. The proof technique (fiber decomposition → uniform counting → ENNReal ratio cancellation) is a reusable template for any combinatorial probability argument whose events have equal-sized preimages: card-shuffles, random projection arguments in coding theory, symmetric group actions on labeled objects. The Boolean closure (complements, unions) confirms the map is a probability-algebra homomorphism on the full power-set algebra, which in ergodic theory language means f is a factor map between discrete probability spaces.
openQuestions: Can this be lifted to MeasureTheory.Measure.map: does a Measurable equal-fiber surjection push `Measure.count` restricted to A to `Measure.count` restricted to T, formalized as `(Measure.count.restrict A).map f = Measure.count.restrict T`?

For non-uniform fiber sizes, is there a characterization of exactly which events P ⊆ T have their uniformOn probability preserved? (Intuition: P must be a union of 'equi-weighted' cosets of the fiber-size partition.)

Does the result extend to infinite sets under a suitable density notion? For sequences with natural density, an equal-density fiber condition might give an analogous Cesàro-mean probability preservation.

Can this theorem be stated as a Mathlib-ready lemma for contribution? The theorem's hypotheses (finite sets, uniform fiber sizes, surjectivity) are clean enough to fit into Mathlib's ProbabilityTheory.uniformOn API — is there prior art to cite or are these genuinely novel lemmas?
